items.title: When voices can be cloned: vocal identity threat and occupational self-efficacy among singers in the era of generative AI audio
items.abstract: Generative AI voice cloning has advanced rapidly, yet its psychological and professional implications for singers remain underexplored. This review synthesizes empirical evidence concerning two central constructs: vocal identity threat, defined as the perceived erosion of the connection between voice and self, and occupational self-efficacy, referring to confidence in maintaining professional competence and value under technological uncertainty. Neurocognitive and behavioral evidence indicates that the human voice functions as a highly self-relevant identity cue supported by self-prioritized processing, body ownership, and multisensory integration. As AI-generated voice clones become increasingly humanlike, questions have emerged about how such technologies may affect singers' perceptions of vocal identity and professional value. Importantly, perceptual discrimination between human and AI-generated voices remains dependent on stimulus characteristics, listener factors, and the availability of prosodic and expressive cues. We argue that three distinctions are critical for interpreting the current evidence: timbral similarity should not be equated with artistic equivalence, increasingly humanlike output does not establish perceptual interchangeability, and the implications of AI may differ depending on whether it substitutes for identity-bearing vocal labor or scaffolds human-controlled performance and creation. Current evidence therefore provides an empirical basis for investigating potential AI-related threats to singers' vocal identity and occupational confidence, but direct singer-specific evidence remains unavailable. Future research should prioritize singer-specific quantitative studies employing longitudinal designs, ecologically valid voice-cloning scenarios, comparison conditions, and direct measures of identity threat and occupational self-efficacy.

items.title: Where Research Ideation Begins: Forward-Citation Supervision for Actionable Limitation Generation
items.abstract: Automated research ideation has advanced rapidly, with multi-agent workflows that generate whole research ideas end to end. These frameworks leave largely unexamined the step that seeds a good idea: identifying an actionable limitation from literature. In this paper, we focus on this first step in the research ideation pipeline. Starting from a pilot study, we find that as large language models (LLMs) scale from 0.6B to 32B parameters, they become far better at recognizing which limitation later work addressed, but no better at generating one, suggesting that the bottleneck lies in the supervision signal rather than model capacity. We therefore construct ActLim-Bench from forward citations, yielding 18,279 evidence-linked supervision triples with human verification. On this signal, we propose a three-stage post-training pipeline: supervised fine-tuning, verifier-filtered rejection-sampling fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with the verifier as an online dense reward. Experimental results show that our method achieves the highest recall score compared to existing methods among all frontier models. We further show that our generated limitations are preferred in 64.9% of non-tied human comparisons and improve downstream ideation systems. We will release our data and code upon publication.

items.title: Who Plans, Who Edits? Verified, Cost-Aware Division of Labor for LLM-Driven Analog Layout Repair
items.abstract: Language-model agents can repair analog layouts when sign-off tools check every edit, but which model should plan a repair, which should edit it, and at what cost remain open questions. In our tool-grounded repair agent, models only choose bounded layout operators; sign-off tools rerun each task's contract checks after every edit, so failing layouts are never accepted. On layout-versus-schematic (LVS), design-rule checking (DRC), and post-layout repairs of three designs (a production high-voltage digital-to-analog converter (DAC), a 5-V oscillator, and a SKY130 operational transconductance amplifier (OTA)) with six tier-matched models from two vendors, 182 blind runs show that cheap models execute plans but rarely succeed alone (the cheapest model: 1 of 11 runs alone, 16 of 17 under a flagship planner; p < 0.001), cheap planners fail more often, and no fixed assignment is cheapest on every task. We propose a learning controller that selects models for each role and the escalation order from the first tool evaluation and updates Bayesian estimates after every attempt. With rules and initial estimates frozen before testing, the controller fixed 7 of 8 episodes on four sealed held-out tasks, matching the OpenAI flagship alone, at 15-40% of the flagship's spend per fix on three tasks but 8% higher spend overall. The cheapest mid-tier model alone fixed 6 of 8 at the lowest overall spend per fix but missed the hardest task. All 32 extracted DAC repairs match the human-guided LVS repair's integral nonlinearity (INL) within 0.005 least significant bits (LSB) at every code.

items.title: Who Speaks, Who Authorizes, Who Acts? Understanding Trust Boundaries in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems exchange messages before acting through tools, but message delivery, signing authority, and tool-side enforcement are separate trust boundaries. We represent them as communication, authorization, and execution structures, and use the authority cut to characterize the smallest independently compromised signer coalition that can construct a policy-valid false-claim proof under stated assumptions. Controlled paired hidden-state studies reveal four distinctions. First, no fixed-message routing contrast across four models meets the prespecified large-effect criterion; when relays rewrite messages, executed false-state action rates vary by model and route configuration. Second, presented source-identity cues do not uniformly increase protected-action selection across three models. Third, on invalid-proof cases, Nemotron and Llama request protected actions in 52.1% and 54.2% of trials, respectively, yet a deterministic tool gate commits none: request-level and commitment-level safety readouts diverge. Finally, a separate single-model authorization check shows that a false claim with a policy-valid compromised-signer proof can pass the gate, since proof validity is not factual truth. These findings motivate evaluating delivered information, qualified authorization, model proposals, and committed actions separately.

items.title: Word-color association from large-scale online data: Methodology and applications
items.abstract: Words and colors are intimately associated in humans, a sign of the close relationship between verbal, linguistic expression and cognition. Word-color association therefore plays an important role in areas of communication such as marketing and literature. Traditional efforts to build a general, scalable, and quantitative mapping of word-color association have often relied on surveys, experiencing difficulties in curating large-scale data sets, enrolling sufficient participants, and excising potential inherent researcher biases in the choice of the words and the colors to be mapped. Even the most recent computational efforts based on Large Language Models (LLMs) do not overcome these problems due to their near-complete lack of transparency in data and methodology that results in low confidence, consistency, and reliability. Here we propose a framework that overcomes these limitations via the use of freely accessible large-scale web image data, and fully transparent and reproducible methods that allow one to build color associations for almost any given word. We also showcase the methodology in action through analyses of color usage in corporate branding and 20th-century Anglo-American poetry. These show that our framework can help form new answers to and perspectives on long-standing questions in communication. Additionally, our framework by design can be readily adopted for use in any language supported by a web image search engine, and its code is freely available in open source; we therefore expect it to contribute towards achieving a universal, multilingual understanding of word-color association.

items.title: XAI and its Applications in Decision Support System
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed decision-making across various industries by enabling systems to analyse large volumes of data and provide intelligent recommendations. However, many modern AI models, particularly deep learning algorithms, function as "black boxes," making it difficult for users to understand how decisions are generated. This lack of transparency limits the adoption of AI in critical domains such as healthcare, finance, law, and business. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has emerged as a promising solution that improves transparency, interpretability, and trust in AI systems. Decision Support Systems (DSS) assist decision-makers by combining data, analytical models, and domain knowledge. Integrating XAI into DSS enables users to understand AI-generated recommendations, thereby improving confidence and accountability. This review paper explores the concepts of XAI, different explanation techniques, and their applications in DSS. The paper also discusses recent research, challenges, limitations, and future research directions

items.title: Zero-Shot Extraction of Structured Clinical Data from Free-Text CT Reports Using Foundational Large Language Models
items.abstract: Introduction. Large language models (LLMs) are being explored for multiple applications in medical research, including medical text classification. Authors of the study evaluated the performance of three off-the-shelf LLMs in classifying unstructured free-text CT pulmonary angiography reports for pulmonary embolism (PE)-related diagnostic labels.Methods. Authors assessed human-labeled CT reports using three LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Llama 3.3 70B, and Llama 3.1 8B) with zero-shot simple and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompts. Classification tasks included acute PE (N = 1,025) and, among reports with PE (n = 660), bilateral PE and large PE.Results. LLMs demonstrated high classification performance for acute PE and bilateral PE but lower performance for large PE. With simple prompts, the highest F1 scores were 97.0% for acute PE (Llama 3.1 8B; sensitivity, 95.6%; specificity, 97.3%), 92.9% for bilateral PE (ChatGPT-4o; sensitivity, 98.0%; specificity, 88.6%), and 72.8% for large PE (ChatGPT-4o; sensitivity, 82.9%; specificity, 82.2%). CoT prompting did not meaningfully improve acute PE classification but provided slight improvements in subclassification performance for bilateral and large PE.Conclusions. Off-the-shelf LLMs can classify free-text CT reports using simple prompt engineering and may facilitate automated data extraction for medical research following appropriate evaluation of classification performance.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

items.abstract: This paper presents a web application for creating and taking quizzes that integrates artificial intelligence into the educational process. Particular emphasis is placed on the automatic generation of quiz questions using AI, significantly accelerating and simplifying the quiz preparation process. In addition, several AI-powered functionalities have been implemented with the aim of enhancing the teaching and learning experience, improving educational outcomes, and increasing the efficiency of both teachers and students.

items.abstract: У статті розглянуто проблему узгодження змісту спеціальної фізичної підготовки майбутніх поліцейських із вимогами професійної діяльності. Мета дослідження - на основі критичного аналізу українських та іноземних публікацій визначити напрями вдосконалення підготовки й оцінювання професійно значущої рухової готовності курсантів. Зіставлено підходи до загального фізичного тестування, професійно орієнтованого тренування та навчання в умовах ситуаційної невизначеності. Показано, що поліпшення окремих фізичних показників саме по собі не підтверджує сформованості комплексної готовності до службових дій. Обґрунтовано доцільність поєднання стандартизованих фізичних тестів із ситуаційним оцінюванням, яке враховує якість рухових дій, комунікацію, обґрунтованість рішень і безпеку. Запропоновано структуру педагогічної моделі, що передбачає вхідне діагностування, диференційоване планування навантаження, поступове ускладнення умов виконання завдань і відстрочений контроль збереження навичок. Визначено обмеження доказової бази: неоднорідність досліджуваних контингентів, невеликі вибірки окремих експериментів, недостатнє висвітлення надійності оцінювання та обмежену кількість спостережень за результатами після завершення навчання. Практичне значення роботи полягає у визначенні критеріїв для перегляду навчальних завдань і процедур педагогічного контролю. Запропонована модель має теоретико-методичний характер і потребує подальшої емпіричної перевірки. References: 1. items.abstract: Occupational accidents and diseases are among the most significant challenges in process industries, particularly in the oil and gas sector, and can lead to considerable human, economic, and environmental consequences. The present study aimed to prioritize strategies for reducing occupational accidents and diseases in Parsian Gas Refining Company, located in Mohr County, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). In terms of purpose, this research is applied, and in terms of methodology, it is descriptive-analytical. The statistical population consisted of 30 experts in the field of occupational health and safety, including HSE specialists of Parsian Gas Refining Company, labor inspectors, and official judiciary experts in occupational accidents, who were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a pairwise comparison questionnaire based on the AHP method. The decision-making criteria included effectiveness in risk reduction, cost-effectiveness, feasibility, legal compliance, and employee acceptance. The alternatives under evaluation comprised engineering controls, administrative controls, training and behavioral safety, and personal protective equipment. The results of the AHP analysis indicated that engineering controls ranked first with a final weight of 0.4654, followed by administrative controls with a weight of 0.2507, training and behavioral safety with a weight of 0.1618, and personal protective equipment with a weight of 0.1221, ranking second, third, and fourth, respectively. The consistency ratio of judgments was obtained as 0.0413, which is lower than the acceptable threshold of 0.1 and indicates satisfactory consistency of the comparisons. The findings of this study can assist managers and safety professionals in selecting the most effective strategies for reducing occupational accidents in the oil and gas industry.

items.abstract: This study aimed to assess ergonomic risks, explore cultural contexts, beliefs, health perceptions, and adaptation patterns, and synthesize health promotion approaches among older lu-mien, an ethnic minority group, women engaged in embroidery. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 23 older Lu-Mien women using the Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA) tool, while qualitative data were obtained through in-depth interviews with 12 key informants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative data were analyzed using thematic content analysis. The findings revealed that participants had a mean ergonomic risk score of 4.48 (S.D. = 1.04). Of the participants, 60.87% were classified as requiring ergonomic intervention, whereas 39.13% required further investigation and monitoring. Most participants reported neck, back, and shoulder pain associated with prolonged forward-bending postures and repetitive work activities. Despite the identified ergonomic risks, many older women perceived such discomfort as a normal consequence of aging and daily work, leading to limited attention to ergonomic prevention practices. Embroidery was found to hold significant cultural, psychological, and social value, serving as a life skill, a marker of cultural identity, and a means of fostering social relationships within the community. Health management practices were largely based on trial-and-error adaptations and reliance on traditional local wisdom, such as Gua Sha or Scraping Therapy, a traditional Chinese medicine treatment. The findings led to the synthesis of culturally appropriate health promotion approaches that integrate ergonomic principles with cultural contexts by using embroidery as a foundation for health promotion, while encouraging movement during work and improving work environments in ways that are compatible with older adults’ lifestyles.

items.title: ‘Too dumb to be Dutch’: learning ability test in Dutch civic integration programme
items.abstract: This study presents an in-depth analysis of the Learning Ability Test (LAT), a new testing tool used in Dutch civic integration. Drawing from theoretical perspectives rooted in Science and Technology Studies, testing studies, and critical migration and integration studies, we conceptualise the test as a sociotechnical actor in the ‘ordering’ processes of contemporary jus linguarum citizenship, where membership is increasingly tied to demonstrable language proficiency. Analysing government documents and interviews with test developers, administrators and test-takers, we reconstruct how the LAT was designed, contested and ultimately stabilised as an ‘objective’, evidence-based tool through various technologies of legitimacy. We show that the LAT does far more than assess linguistic potential. Applied at the start of the integration trajectory, it sorts subjects into differentiated learning routes and citizenship horizons, functioning as an internal raciolinguistic border that silently ranks their worth and presumed capacity for ‘self-reliance’. The analysis highlights how the test’s thresholds, categories and discretionary space translate political and moral judgements into the language of measurement, obscuring the racialised and discriminatory work they perform. We conclude that this ostensibly neutral classification tool not only reproduces but also deepens hierarchies of desirable and undesirable citizens, with significant consequences for access to naturalisation and full membership.

items.title: “Boo, Get off the Stage!” Lessons from Robot Adaptation to Failed Jokes in a Robot Comedy Experiment that Compared Different Room-Reading Techniques
items.abstract: Public-facing social robots, including robotic comedians, need to recognize onlooker reactions and repair failures when an interaction falls flat. In the presented work, we use stand-up comedy as a structured and fast-paced testbed to partially address this broader challenge of perceiving and adapting to failures; the robot can deliver a silly joke, observe an immediate audience response, and select an appropriate follow-up within a short interaction loop. We compare three room-reading strategies for informing post-joke adaptation by a fully autonomous NAO robot comedian. The strategies use crowd audio cues, visual facial reactions, or spoken audience feedback to select repair-oriented responses. We evaluated these three condition approaches in 19 total live performances (split between conditions) with \(N\) =80 total participants and measured experience using performance-level joke ratings, perceived social closeness, and social attribute ratings, along with post-performance group interviews. Across conditions, outcomes were broadly positive and we found no statistically significant differences between strategies, which suggests that each modality can support viable adaptation while capturing different forms of audience engagement. The study's manipulation check and interviews also showed that presumed robot adaptivity mode mattered, especially for the verbal strategy, which could be compelling when audiences engaged but was less reliably recognized when groups were quiet. This work supports flexible room-reading tactics for failure repair in public-facing robots while highlighting the importance of making a robot's adaptive behavior understandable in the moment.

items.title: "Do You Trust It... or Check It?": Exploring Children's Verification Behaviors in Game-Based Human-AI Collaboration
items.abstract: Children are increasingly interacting with AI agents in learning and problem-solving contexts, where AI suggestions may appear fluent, helpful, and socially engaging. However, children may not always be able to judge whether such suggestions are accurate, incomplete, or misleading. This paper presents a game-based human-AI collaboration probe designed to examine how children verify AI suggestions during task-based interaction. The system embeds AI suggestions within a biological knowledge reasoning game and compares three Agent interaction styles: partner-like, tool-like, and dual-state Agent. Instead of treating trust as a static post-task attitude, this study focuses on children's situated verification behaviors, including acceptance, evidence checking, questioning, revision, and continued AI use. A preliminary evaluation with children aged 8-10 combined interaction logs, post-task ratings, and semi-structured interviews. The findings suggest that Agent style shaped children's engagement and response pathways: partner-like interaction tended to support direct questioning, while tool-like interaction was more associated with evidence seeking. Children generally viewed AI as useful but fallible, and their questioning behaviors varied in reasoning depth. The study contributes design insights for supporting children's critical, reflective, and evidence-based use of AI in collaborative tasks.

items.title: “I Didn’t Know That was Plagiarism”: EFL Students' AI-Giarism in a Pesantren-Based Higher Education
items.abstract: The rise of generative AI (Gen-AI) tools has blurred the ethical boundaries of academic writing, shifting the definition of plagiarism from traditional methods to AI-based plagiarism (AI-giarism). English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students are the most vulnerable people to fall into this practice due to second language writing anxiety, which drives dependency on AI as a shortcut. This study aims to examine the levels of knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported AI-based plagiarism practices among EFL students at a pesantren-based higher education institution. Employing a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were collected using a validated 51-item questionnaire adapted from Phyo et al. (2023), distributed to 99 English education students at a pesantren-based higher education in East Java, Indonesia, via Google Forms. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman’s correlation, multiple linear regression, and binary logistic regression. Result revealed a moderate level of knowledge (mean = 9.63/17; 56.6%), with the greatest weakness in understanding that AI-generated text passing Turnitin still constitutes plagiarism (only 33.3% correct). Attitudes rejecting plagiarism were at a moderate level (mean = 91.24/135; 67.6%), with the self-justification subscale scoring the lowest (55.5%). A total of 50.5% of respondents had engaged in at least one act of AI-giarism. Knowledge score emerged as the sole significant independent predictor of AI plagiarism behavior (AOR = 0.764;95% CI [0.62-0.94]; p = 0.012). These findings reveal the “Pesantren Paradox”: a conflict between strong religious moral capital and limited digital-ethical literacy, which creates a loophole for unintended AI-giarism.

items.abstract: This article examines the case of the feldsher Juho Sairio in late nineteenth-century Finland and analyses the boundaries of authority between physicians and feldshers within a changing medical culture. Sairio worked extensively in occupational health care at the Karhula industrial works in a context where medical services were scarce and expensive. He treated thousands of patients, prepared medicines, and kept a medical casebook, yet his activities became the subject of official investigation and legal scrutiny. The article demonstrates that feldshers occupied an ambiguous intermediate position between formal medicine and informal healing practices. While their duties were officially defined as belonging mainly to “minor surgery”, in practice they often operated far more broadly, particularly in industrial communities and remote areas. Sairio’s case illustrates how the boundaries of professional authority were not fixed but were negotiated in response to practical needs, local conditions, and interactions among different actors. In the ensuing trial, a central issue was whether Sairio had exceeded his authority by treating internal diseases, prescribing medicines, and charging fees. He was convicted of practising medicine without a licence and of violating regulations governing the sale of poisons. The case reveals that the consolidation of the medical profession’s boundaries was shaped not only by concerns about patient safety but also by economic interests and professional competition. The article’s main argument is that the boundaries of health care are historically produced through negotiation and everyday practice. The case of Sairio highlights both the central yet underappreciated role of feldshers in everyday health care and the ways in which semi-official practitioners adapted to changing regulatory and market environments.

items.title: $Stakeholder perspectives on the future of trucking in an automated world
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded into vehicle automation and fleet operations, the U.S. trucking industry faces opportunities and challenges. These technologies promise safety and efficiency gains, but also raise underexplored questions regarding workforce transitions, training, and regulatory frameworks. This study investigated how stakeholders across the U.S. trucking industry perceive the integration of AI systems, including advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and automated commercial motor vehicles (ACMVs), and the implications for safety, operational practices, and workforce adaptation. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 33 U.S.-based participants representing five stakeholder groups: truck drivers, trucking companies, truck driving schools, technology developers, and policymakers. Data were thematically analyzed and mapped onto the sociotechnical systems framework (environment, organizations, workers, tasks, and tools & technologies). Six themes emerged: (1) Feasibility of AI-Enabled Systems, spanning regulation, training and licensing, infrastructure, and human–technology teaming; (2) Benefits such as increased safety, efficiency, workload balance, and industry appeal; (3) Workforce Impacts related to job availability, role transitions, and satisfaction; (4) Technology Perceptions characterized by trust and skepticism; (5) Industry Practices including recruitment, training, and fleet management; and (6) Innovation involving automation progress, and deployment. Most subthemes were shared across all five groups, while others were raised by a subset or a single group, revealing both convergence and divergence in how stakeholders understand AI integration. Stakeholders identified AI’s potential to improve safety and efficiency, but raised concerns about job displacement, regulatory gaps, and human oversight. This study provides insights for system design, human-technology interaction, training, workforce adaptation and regulatory frameworks.

items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in second-language (L2) writing assessment. However, substantial disparities persist in how different architectures operationalize shared scoring criteria. This study investigates model-specific assessment asymmetry across ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.5 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3, and evaluates whether a calibrated multi-LLM consensus framework can mitigate these scoring discrepancies. Forty argumentative essays composed by Chinese EFL learners were independently evaluated by the three models using a standardized prompt and an analytic rubric encompassing task relevance, clarity of ideas, coherence, and accuracy, benchmarked against human mean scores. Individual models and ensemble configurations were systematically validated across 100 iterations of five-fold nested cross-validation. Cross-model comparisons revealed that inter-model divergence varied significantly by dimension, exhibiting pronounced asymmetry in holistic ratings and task relevance compared to clarity of ideas, coherence, and accuracy. The full consensus framework—integrating model-specific calibration, error-based weighting, and meta-calibration—yielded an RMSE of 1.160 and an MAE of 0.889, relative to 1.144 and 0.874 for unweighted averaging. The paired RMSE difference of 0.016 (95% case-cluster bootstrap CI [−0.114, 0.149]) indicated no statistically significant advantage in overall predictive accuracy over equal weighting. Nevertheless, the calibrated framework achieved superior bias mitigation, evidenced by a reduced absolute mean bias and a narrower median-split residual gap. Supplementary analyses further delineated direct inter-model discrepancies and proficiency-dependent residual bias. These findings demonstrate that model-specific evaluative asymmetries transcend simple mean-level shifts, and that while calibration-driven consensus enhances bias regulation across score bands, this error control does not automatically translate into improved global predictive precision.

items.title: A Conversational AI Framework for Teacher Training
items.abstract: This paper introduces ETQ-AI (Effective Teaching Questionnaire—Artificial Intelligence), a conversational AI framework designed to support teacher professional development by identifying pedagogical misconceptions and fostering critical reflection. Building on Evidence-Informed Education (EIE) principles, the system integrates a 50-item diagnostic questionnaire with an automated, Gemini-driven Explainable AI (XAI) feedback layer. When teachers complete the diagnostic form, they receive personalized feedback and can engage in dialogic interactions with Google Gemini to explore the underlying meta-analytic evidence (e.g., Hattie’s effect sizes, Cognitive Load Theory) or argue personal objections. We evaluated system fidelity against an expert panel benchmark (N=64 items) and conducted a pilot evaluation with 123 educators (70 primary teachers, 40 secondary teachers, 13 school leaders) recruited at an EIE conference. Gemini demonstrated high alignment with expert evaluations (97%), matching or exceeding static baseline feedback in user satisfaction (Mean = 4.1/5 vs. 3.8/5). Qualitative thematic analysis of 34 participant objections revealed key areas of tension, particularly around contextual constraints and pedagogical subjectivity. While the findings validate the technical proof-of-concept, system usability, and user engagement of ETQ-AI as an interactive scaffolding interface, we emphasize that this pilot study measures user perceptions and conversational patterns rather than direct pre/post shifts in critical reflection or classroom instructional practice.

items.title: A Critical Epistemological Audit of Early Evidence Syntheses in Generative AI Educational Research: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: The rapid emergence of ChatGPT in education was accompanied by an equally rapid proliferation of meta-analyses synthesizing its effects on educational outcomes. We conducted a systematic epistemological audit of the first wave of these meta-analyses, evaluating both their methodological and reporting quality and the primary evidence they synthesized. We included meta-analyses published after the release of ChatGPT that quantitatively synthesized its effects on educational outcomes. Five meta-analyses comprising 87 unique primary studies met our inclusion criteria. We also reconstructed their quantitative evidence base and conducted exploratory three-level random-effects meta-analyses to examine effect magnitude, heterogeneity, and robustness, and how these varied with theoretically and methodologically relevant characteristics. The five meta-analyses generally searched multiple databases, specified eligibility criteria, and examined heterogeneity and potential publication bias, but showed limitations in independent screening and coding, preregistration, open data and code, and transparent reporting. The underlying primary evidence likewise showed methodological and reporting limitations and substantial conceptual heterogeneity. Among 69 classifiable primary studies, 79.7% assessed performance exclusively, whereas only 11.6% assessed learning exclusively. The reconstructed meta-analysis yielded a positive average effect (g = 0.83, 95% CI [0.68, 0.97]), but heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 94.06%; 95% prediction interval [−0.75, 2.41]), and estimates were markedly attenuated in sensitivity analyses addressing small-study and selection effects. Although positive effects remained among stronger studies assessing learning, increasingly stringent quality criteria rapidly reduced the evidence base, limiting the certainty and generalizability of conclusions about learning effects. Overall, our findings caution against interpreting a single pooled estimate as a stable general effect of ChatGPT on learning and highlight the need for more rigorous, conceptually precise, transparent, and reproducible research.

items.title: A Critical Review of Applications, Agency, and the Imperative of Pedagogical Governance for Educators at the Center of Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved from a marginal interest to a fundamental structural element of modern higher education. Even though AI applications are growing quickly, including profiling and prediction, intelligent tutoring systems (ITS), automated assessment, and adaptive personalization, the academic literature has mostly been written from the points of view of computer science and engineering, which focus on how well technology works instead of how it can be used for teaching, how teachers can use it, and how it can be used in an ethical way. This chapter revisits and significantly expands the foundational systematic review by Zawacki-Richter et al. (2019), incorporating an analysis of the transformative emergence of generative AI systems post-2022. Based on 146 sources of recent empirical studies, policy papers, and theoretical works, the chapter contends that the educational value of AI is not intrinsic to its technical design nor assured by adoption rates, but is formed through the interpretive, curricular, and ethical efforts of human educators. Based on a review of more than 30 peer-reviewed sources, the chapter looks at four main areas where AI is used, questions the structural marginalization of educators in research and governance, and proposes an educator-centered framework for responsible AI integration. It concludes that, in an era when AI increasingly permeates the day-to-day fabric of academic life, repositioning educators from peripheral end-users to central theoretical and practical actors is not merely an intellectual corrective – it is a structural imperative for preserving the educational purposes of the university.

items.title: A Data-Driven Smart University Framework for Sustainable Internationalisation at Home: A PLS-SEM Study in Vietnamese Higher Education
items.abstract: Internationalisation at Home is increasingly recognised as an alternative to conventional physical mobility, offering opportunities to broaden equitable access to knowledge and promote sustainable practices in higher education. This study develops and empirically tests a data-driven smart university framework as an integrative model for examining the structural relationships between technological foundations and the sustainable implementation of Internationalisation at Home. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed, using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 312 managers and faculty members involved in transnational education programmes in Vietnam. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings support the proposed structural relationships within the model. Specifically, integrated data infrastructure has a positive relationship with faculty digital competence. An ethical data governance framework and the adoption of learning analytics and artificial intelligence are also positively associated with the quality of Internationalisation at Home. In turn, the quality of Internationalisation at Home has a statistically significant positive relationship with perceived institutional sustainability. The study provides empirical evidence of the structural links between digital technological innovation and the sustainability of higher education internationalisation. The findings offer a basis for reconsidering institutional resource allocation strategies in developing countries, with greater priority given to integrated data architectures, digital capability development, and responsible data governance.

items.title: A design space for AI integration in early-stage production plant planning
items.abstract: Early-stage production plant planning is characterised by evolving requirements, incomplete process definitions, and information distributed across documents, engineering models, and planning tools. Introducing artificial intelligence in this setting raises a fundamental question: what must be considered before a specific application, data model, or technical solution can be defined? Existing research typically starts from an already identified planning task, a selected artificial intelligence method, or an available technical infrastructure. It therefore provides limited guidance for structuring the initial need and determining how artificial intelligence should enter planning work. This paper develops a design space that addresses this early decision problem. Literature from factory planning, production planning, collaboration between humans and artificial intelligence, semantic technologies, and digital planning was compared to derive five dimensions: planning scope, information structure, authority to modify planning results, connection to planning tools and data, and functional contribution. Data quality, organisational roles, governance, and interaction are considered as additional conditions. Application to process failure mode and effects analysis shows how the appropriate configuration changes as preliminary process information develops into a maintained planning record. The design space helps planners, artificial-intelligence specialists, and system engineers specify implementation requirements before selecting a particular technical solution.

items.title: A Diamond Grain Lost in the Sandy River Bank - The Illusion of Wisdom in the Age of AI, Data Truncation, and the Erasure of Absolute Truth
items.abstract: This concept paper bridges classical Theravada Buddhist epistemological frameworks with mathematical information theory to diagnose a fundamental structural flaw in contemporary artificial intelligence alignment paradigms. Utilizing the classical allegory of the Nakhasikha Sutta—the comparison between a few sand grains on a fingernail and the vast sands of a riverbank—I model how rare, absolute spiritual and philosophical insights are systematically annihilated by modern frontier model ingestion architectures. I demonstrate that modern AI training dynamics rely on mathematical optimization algorithms (such as gradient clipping and softmax vector dilution) that treat low-frequency, high-dimensional truths as statistical outliers, subjecting them to severe data truncation and lossy semantic compression. Consequently, modern frontier networks function as ungrounded symbol manipulators whose latent representation spaces undergo systemic collapse toward the majority distribution of mundane internet prose, rendering them structurally deaf to genuine deontological or metaphysical principles. Finally, the paper demonstrates that post-hoc alignment protocols, such as Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), merely construct a superficial, deceptive compliance layer over a compromised, materialistic baseline dataset rather than inducing authentic value alignment. I argue instead for a radical return to strict epistemic hygiene at the absolute genesis of development, isolating the initialization vector within an immutable database of verified wisdom.

items.title: A força da Marrom:: atos performativos e regimes de verdade na imagem de Alcione
items.abstract: This article examines the circulation of digital statements linking the Brazilian singer Alcione to a recent political event known as macumbinha. Drawing on Foucault (1979; 2008), the study approaches these materials as discursive practices embedded in regimes of truth and shaped by sociotechnical dispositifs that organize visibility and meaning-making. Using a qualitative approach grounded in archaeogenealogy, the study analyzes a corpus of social media posts, images, user comments, and news coverage collected from digital platforms. The statements were selected according to their recurrence, engagement, and diversity of formats. The analysis is organized around three analytical axes: symbolic legitimation, performative acts, and discursive regularities. The findings show that Alcione's public image contributes to the stabilization of political narratives while fostering forms of belonging and the constitution of truth.

items.title: A Framework for Teaching the Responsible and Effective Use of Generative AI in Statistics and Data Science
items.abstract: The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) following the public release of tools such as ChatGPT has begun to reshape how students engage with coding, statistical analysis, and written communication in higher education. Growing use of conversational AI systems creates opportunities for learning alongside challenges around reliability, transparency, privacy, and appropriate academic and professional practice, highlighting the need for structured education in their responsible use. This paper presents a framework for teaching the responsible and effective use of generative AI in statistics and data science. The framework is organised around four areas: Understanding, Development, Reporting, and Safety, covering conceptual foundations, practical interaction within analytical workflows, documentation and transparency, and issues including reliability, bias, privacy, and ethics. Its design draws on emerging work in AI literacy and established principles from statistics and data science education, and was further refined through workshop and conference activities and participant feedback. The framework has been implemented across multiple settings, including a massive open online course, short training sessions, and undergraduate and postgraduate skills-based teaching. We use these experiences to identify broader design considerations for educators, including the value of authentic analytical tasks, critical evaluation of generated outputs, integrated consideration of responsible practice, and flexibility as generative AI technologies continue to evolve.

items.title: A Fuzzy Knowledge-Inference Framework for AI-Adoption Risk Assessment in Automotive SMEs
items.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises in the automotive supply base face mounting pressure to adopt artificial intelligence, yet they are least able to absorb the consequences of misscoped adoption. Assessing this risk means reasoning under vagueness: Data maturity, workforce skill, financial capacity, and above all safety and regulatory readiness are graded, interdependent judgments that crisp, compensatory instruments discard. This paper proposes the fuzzy knowledge inference framework, a two-stage rough–fuzzy framework. Eight automotive-specific risk factors are represented as linguistic variables over an information system; rough-set analysis establishes their nonredundancy; and a hierarchical fuzzy inference process—anchored, compliance-weighted, and noncompensatory—yields an interpretable risk index. Using no primary human data, it is well calibrated at its anchors, monotone in favorability, and rank-convergent with two independent instruments, while escalating the profiles a compensatory model would understate. Its contribution to the literature on AI-adoption risk assessment for automotive SMEs is the noncompensatory treatment of safety and regulatory readiness.

items.title: A Governance Framework for Operationalising Responsible AI Use in Students’ Research Projects: Illustrations from Viet Nam
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in students’ research projects for literature searching, idea development, drafting, language editing, information processing, and research planning. These uses can support research learning, but they also raise academic integrity concerns, including unverifiable sources, fabricated references, undeclared AI assistance, over-reliance on AI-generated outputs, unclear authorship, and unfair assessment. This conceptual paper argues that responsible AI use in students’ research projects cannot be secured through individual AI literacy or general guidance alone. Higher education institutions also need governance mechanisms that make AI use transparent, verifiable, assessable, and accountable. Using targeted literature identification and structured conceptual synthesis, the paper maps recurring governance problems to normative principles, institutional requirements, and operational mechanisms. It proposes a five-component framework corresponding to five governance functions: policy (boundary setting), transparency (traceability), assessment (evaluability), audit (assurance), and guidance/support (capability building). Viet Nam is used as an illustrative emerging AI governance context, where national policy directions on digital competence and AI are developing but operational mechanisms for student research remain under-specified. The framework and associated tools are presented as adaptable design artefacts for future institutional testing rather than as validated interventions.

items.title: A Literature Review on the Sensor Network Design Problem Applied to Chemical Processes
items.abstract: In the present paper, a comprehensive review of methodologies for the optimal placement of measurement devices in chemical processes, commonly referred to as the sensor network design problem (SNDP), is presented. The SNDP is a combinatorial optimization problem of paramount importance in process design, monitoring, control, and data reconciliation, as sensor placement directly affects estimability, precision, reliability, and fault detectability. In addition to surveying solution strategies for SNDP, this review examines the closely related variable classification problem, which constitutes a fundamental building block in the systematic development of sensor networks. The evolution of the field is analyzed, highlighting early structural search approaches, subsequent optimization-based formulations relying on relaxation and decomposition techniques, and heuristic and metaheuristic strategies. The strengths and limitations of these methodological classes are discussed with respect to problem size and computational complexity. Moreover, this review identified a novel strategy to solve SNDPs based on machine learning algorithms. Finally, future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the growing need for scalable frameworks capable of addressing increasingly large and automated industrial systems. As computational capabilities continue to advance and process plants transition toward highly digitalized environments, research efforts devoted to efficient and robust SNDP methodologies are expected to intensify. In this context, Large Language Models (LLMs) can play a transformative role.

items.title: A misinformation playbook sharpens judgement without breeding cynicism
items.abstract: Misinformation harms public health and democracy, and generative artificial intelligence now writes falsehoods as persuasive as people's. Defences range from fact-checking individual claims to training people to resist falsehoods. Yet many claims are too new to check, and interventions that teach doubt can reduce belief in truth too. We propose a defence that targets not the facts of each claim but the persuasion strategies that recur across them. Here we show that learning misinformation's persuasion playbook, mapped from 214,646 fact-checked claims in 51 languages, can sharpen human and machine judgement of claims they know little about, without making either more cynical about true claims. The playbook spans social influence, information manipulation and emotional appeals, combined around a core of fear, conspiracy and fabrication. Briefed with it, plus a reminder that persuasion is not proof of falsehood, a language model better distinguished true from machine-generated false claims about events after its training data. In a pre-registered experiment, the same briefing improved people's discernment of claims they reported as unfamiliar and left their belief in true claims unchanged. Averaged over all claims, the gain was not statistically significant. Because it targets what recurs, this defence need not wait for claim-specific fact-checks.

items.title: A multilevel framework of human–AI knowledge work and its epistemic consequences for organizational decision-making
items.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative AI into knowledge work faster than they are adapting the epistemic controls on which knowledge work depends. Existing scholarship has examined the resulting risks predominantly one level at a time (individual reliance and calibration, workflow and oversight design, or institutional legitimacy), and although several traditions acknowledge interactions across actors, routines and institutions, those interactions are rarely theorized as a single cross-level process. Guided by three research questions (how epistemic failures propagate across levels, when such dynamics compound or reverse, and how they could be measured), this paper argues that this insufficient integration becomes consequential under generative AI and develops a framework that extends, rather than replaces, existing multilevel perspectives. We introduce the EPIC (Epistemic Process In Co-production) framework, a multilevel model connecting calibration quality and judgment preservation at the micro level, workflow configuration and oversight architecture at the meso level, and epistemic authority and knowledge legitimacy at the macro level. The framework was developed through a theory-building review of 295 papers retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science (Stage 1, 2018–2026; Stage 2 targeted stream searches, 2004–2026), with per-dimension inter-rater reliability ranging from κ = 0.70 to κ = 0.88. Six constructs and seven testable propositions are advanced, including a provisional four-stage process model of epistemic lock-in in which cognitive legitimacy formation progressively removes the detection capacity that correction requires. Empirical analogues from aviation automation, clinical decision support, satellite navigation, algorithmic hiring and accounting automation establish mechanism plausibility, and we discuss how workforce age and career stage condition these dynamics. We set out four alternative field-level trajectories with leading indicators, map the macro-level constructs onto operative governance instruments, and provide an operationalization roadmap, a worked illustration and a draft diagnostic instrument to support empirical testing.

items.title: A qualitative exploration of climate change effects on study habits and academic engagement of Jagannath University students
items.abstract: This study explores the effects of climate change-induced stresses on students’ study habits and academic engagement at Jagannath University in Old Dhaka, Bangladesh. In a congested and climate-vulnerable metropolitan core, students are frequently disrupted by excessive heat, waterlogging, flooding, and worsening air quality. Using purposive sampling, the study included 38 in-depth interviews, 2 focus group discussions, and 5 key informant interviews across 38 departments of Jagannath University. The analysis was guided by an integrated theoretical framework combining Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, Lazarus and Folkman’s Stress and Coping Theory, and the Student Engagement Framework. These perspectives collectively explain how climate-related stressors operate across environmental systems, how students appraise and respond to stress, and how study habits shape behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement. Findings revealed that environmental stressors directly affect concentration, sleep quality, attendance, and motivation, while institutional constraints exacerbate academic difficulties. Students employ coping methods such as modifying study times, locating cooler spaces, and utilizing digital resources, though these adaptations vary across socioeconomic groups. The study provides context-specific qualitative evidence linking climate vulnerability to students’ lived academic experiences and coping responses. The findings highlight the need for climate-resilient infrastructure, flexible academic arrangements, and institutional support to safeguard academic continuity and student well-being. Finally, by bridging climate vulnerability and higher education resilience, this study supports the Sustainable Development Goals on quality education (SDG 4), sustainable cities (SDG 11), and climate action (SDG 13).

items.title: A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
items.abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation.

items.title: A Study on the Current Status of Cash Logistics and Future Analysis Based on Artificial Intelligence and Industry 5.0
items.abstract: The significance of logistics and SCM has grown due to intense global competition, disaster and the future pandemics. Additionally, the high cost of logistics processes is also increasing the cost and environmental impact of production. This study analyses the current state of research in the field of cash logistics and identifies future development trends based on methodological findings. In the course of the present study, a total of 78 academic articles published between 2006 and 2024 and retrieved from the WoS, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar databases were examined. The primary analytical approach employed was bibliometric mapping and thematic content analysis, supported by MAXQDA and VOSviewer. The findings indicate that the literature focuses primarily on operations research, constrained vehicle routing, AI-based ATM demand forecasting, and the optimization of physical security risks. The analysis results demonstrate that ML and ANN have a significant impact on cost minimization and operational accuracy. In view of these findings, specific recommendations have been developed for industry research and applications. In accordance with the points, it is recommended that human-machine collaboration be strengthened within the framework of Industry 5.0. Furthermore, dynamic optimization algorithms such as deep reinforcement learning, blockchain-based security protocols, and autonomous vehicle systems should be integrated into cash networks.

items.title: A study on three-stage integration of generative artificial intelligence in architectural design based on human-in-the-loop
items.abstract: The swift advancement of artificial intelligence has posed new demands on the architectural industry’s transformation. Generative AI (GAI) enables the digitization of architectural design experience, offering fresh inspiration for architectural scheme generation. This study develops a human-in-the-loop three-phase framework that distinguishes concept generation, scheme deepening, and result expression while adding explicit decision gates and cross-cutting controls for architectural knowledge, performance verification, data provenance, and professional accountability. This study starts by leveraging VOSviewer software to visualize and analyze keyword co-occurrences in GAI-related literature, summarizing GAI’s development trends and hotspots. Then, it outlines GAI’s application stages in architectural design, namely concept generation, scheme deepening, and result expression. It also lists 20 generative design software useful for architectural scheme design. Subsequently, taking Midjourney, NOAH, and Stable Diffusion as examples, it explores GAI’s specific application scenarios across these three design stages. Finally, it proposes a new architectural design model shaped by GAI. The contribution is not a new sequence of conventional design stages, but an operational phase-control matrix that specifies inputs, outputs, human decisions, verification requirements, and feedback loops. It accelerates inspiration image generation, thereby influencing design thinking and processes, meanwhile it provides a cautious, reproducible framework for selecting and governing GAI tools in architectural design.

items.title: A systematic and critical review of artificial intelligence applications for enhancing well stimulation operations and sustainable reservoir management
items.abstract: Well stimulation remains essential for improving reservoir productivity, but conventional workflows are constrained by geological heterogeneity, limited data, and dependence on empirical correlations. This systematic and comparative review examines artificial-intelligence applications in hydraulic fracturing, acidizing, sand control, and ultrasonic stimulation, focusing on 2020–2025 while selectively considering earlier foundational studies. The quantitative synthesis of 23 key application studies identified 11 studies on acidizing and acid fracturing (47.8%), 8 on hydraulic fracturing (34.8%), 3 on sand control (13.0%), and 1 on ultrasonic stimulation (4.3%). Neural-network architectures were reported in 16 studies (69.6%), while tree-based learners or ensembles appeared in 13 studies (56.5%); these categories overlap because several studies compared multiple algorithms. Among studies reporting numerical performance, R2 values for acidizing-related regression tasks ranged from 0.82 to 0.96, while reported classification accuracies for selected acidizing and sand-control applications ranged from 87.5% to above 90%. These values were not statistically pooled because the studies used different prediction targets, data scales, validation procedures, and performance definitions. Tree-based ensembles and neural networks currently dominate fracture-design and acidizing applications, whereas reinforcement learning, hybrid optimization, and physics-informed approaches remain less frequently investigated. Field-scale and cross-field validation are limited, particularly for sand control and ultrasonic stimulation, for which the available evidence is predominantly laboratory- or simulation-based. The principal barriers to operational deployment are proprietary and small datasets, inconsistent validation, limited interpretability, and uncertain model transferability. Future research should prioritize benchmark datasets, standardized reporting, external field validation, explainable and physics-constrained models, and carefully evaluated closed-loop stimulation systems. items.title: A Systematic and Validated Translation of the Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale to Chinese
items.abstract: The Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale (PETS) allows evaluation of empathic behavior in intelligent systems, a concept increasingly applied in human-AI interaction, particularly in emotional and mental health support applications. To support intercultural research and development, PETS is already available in multiple languages, as research suggests cultural and language-based differences in the expression and perception of empathy. Given the substantial Chinese-speaking population and the growing focus on cross-cultural HCI research, we present a validated translation of PETS into Putonghua (Mandarin) with Simplified Chinese. Based on established back-translation methodologies as used in previous PETS translations, our process included multiple independent translations, expert panel reviews, and empirical testing with a total of N=400 participants from an English and a Chinese sample. Through confirmatory factor analysis and invariance testing we show that the Chinese PETS retains the original two-factor structure with high reliability, with support for configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Beyond validation, empathic system behavior was rated equivalently across languages, while non-empathic behavior drew substantially higher ratings from Chinese participants, suggesting its absence is read less consistently across cultures than its presence. This validated Chinese version enables researchers and practitioners to assess empathy perceptions among Chinese-speaking users, supporting culturally appropriate empathic technology development.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Hallucination Mitigation in Large Language Models Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become widely used for question answering, education, research, summarization and information support. Despite their usefulness, LLMs may generate false, unsupported or inconsistent information, commonly described as hallucination. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this reliability problem by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge sources and supplying it to the language model as contextual evidence before generating a response. This paper studies the role of RAG in reducing factual hallucinations through a review of existing research and a 50 question pilot comparison of responses generated with and without retrieval support. The submitted report records 49 of 50 responses as correct without RAG and all 50 as correct with RAG; it separately presents a clearly labelled illustrative distribution of 46/3/1 versus 48/2/0 for demonstrating response categories. The distinction is retained to avoid presenting illustrative values as observed experimental results. The study also examines limitations including poor retrieval, unreliable sources, incomplete context and incorrect interpretation of retrieved evidence. The paper concludes that RAG is a practical hallucination-reduction approach, but it should be combined with high-quality retrieval, evidence verification and human oversight for critical applications.

items.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
items.abstract: We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon. Each agent controlled a player via an open-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in-game chat and shared memory. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic. The agents planned, wrote, and debugged every program themselves. Researchers could watch the run on a live dashboard and pause or stop it at any time, but they had no cause to intervene. Starting from a randomly generated world on Easy difficulty, the team wrote 2,783 programs and defeated the dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, dying 605 times along the way. To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans. Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day. Complex real-world software engineering and enterprise tasks demand the same long-horizon coding and multi-agent coordination. We describe the setup, how the run unfolded, the team's strategies (dividing the work, sharing what they learned, recovering each other's items), and the limits of the result.

items.title: A transdisciplinary AI-based framework for usability evaluation in digital health systems
items.abstract: Introduction. As healthcare systems undergo rapid digital transformation, the usability of clinical and patient-facing technologies has become critical to adoption, user satisfaction, and patient safety. Traditional usability evaluation methods are limited in capturing the real-time cognitive, emotional, and behavioural complexities of interaction in high-stakes environments. Method. This study presents a transdisciplinary evaluation of an AI-augmented usability framework for healthcare interfaces. The framework integrates methodologies from artificial intelligence, cognitive science, usability engineering, and clinical practice, incorporating eye-tracking analytics, machine learning-based confusion prediction, and natural language processing (NLP) sentiment analysis. Forty participants, including healthcare professionals and patients, completed standardized tasks using either traditional or AI-enhanced evaluation methods. Analysis. Comparative performance across both groups was assessed using usability metrics including System Usability Scale (SUS) scores, task completion time, error rate, and task success rate. AI-based analytics—eye-tracking data, NLP sentiment scoring, and confusion prediction models—were used to generate additional insights. Statistical analysis confirmed significant differences in usability outcomes between groups. Results. The AI-enhanced evaluation significantly outperformed traditional methods in all core usability metrics. The machine learning model achieved 89% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.88. Sentiment analysis correlated strongly with self-reported satisfaction, and eye-tracking highlighted areas of cognitive friction. Conclusion. Transdisciplinary collaboration produced a novel, adaptive usability evaluation framework that offers real-time, emotionally aware insights. This replicable model enhances user-centred design and supports safer, more effective digital health technologies.

items.title: A unified multi-domain framework for hallucination detection and reliability evaluation in large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models which consist of models like GPT5 from OpenAI, Claude Sonnet from Anthropic, Google’s Gemini are known for their reasoning capability, ability to summarize, cybersecurity analysis and other features. However, their reliability could be an issue particularly when dealing with ambiguous or hostile user input prompts. These kinds of attacks could lead to soft failures like false citations, hallucinations, and problematic suggestions. Current benchmarks (eg: TruthfulQA, AdvGLUE, and JailbreakBench) assess discrete aspects of robustness but are unable to identify multi-domain, conversational vulnerabilities that come up in practical applications. This paper introduces a novel dataset called MDH-Bench, a benchmark comprising 400 prompts that were specifically created to assess how reliably Large Language Models perform when they are provided with adversarial but natural and even tricky real-world queries. The benchmark covers eight types of challenges. They are numerical reasoning traps, security-sensitive defaults, historical and temporal inconsistencies, fictional research scenarios, contradictory context mixing, ethical provocations, and prompt-injection attempts. To monitor reliability in a holistic way, we present a Unified Multi-Domain Reliability Evaluation Framework that brings together several key metrics like accuracy, hallucination rate, hallucination degree (HD), unsafe output rate, and contradiction rate. A systematic assessment of four high-performance LLMs (GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V3.1) was conducted under controlled, manual, multi-annotator settings. The findings indicate that although overall accuracy is more than 88% in all models, hallucinations are still present both at high frequency and severity level. The results of our investigation showed that solely relying on accuracy is not enough for evaluating the reliability of a system. MDH-Bench and the combined reliability scoring system give a wide-ranging, adaptable base for the assessment and enhancement of trust in future LLMs for real-world applications.

items.title: Abstracts or full text? Evaluating input scope and computational efficiency in biomedical lay summarization
items.abstract: Biomedical research articles are mainly written for experts and often contain terms that are difficult for the general public to understand. Automated lay summarization has become a solution to make biomedical knowledge easier for patients and the public to understand. However, generating lay summaries from full-text articles requires more computing power because the articles are long and costly to process. Fine-tuning large language models for this task also requires substantial resources. This study asks two questions: (1) whether abstracts contain enough information to produce lay summaries as good as those based on full-text articles, and (2) whether few-shot learning performs as well as task-specific fine-tuning. The study used two public biomedical lay summarization datasets and two recent models, evaluated for readability, factual consistency, semantic similarity, and runtime efficiency. Results show that abstract-based summarization performs better overall. Across both datasets and models, abstract fine-tuning is 4.70 times faster, while abstract zero- and few-shot prompting is 5.31 times faster than full-text methods. These results show that abstract-based prompting reduces runtime cost while maintaining lay summary quality.

items.title: Accelerated Dataflow: scaling inference in streaming data analytics with efficiency
items.abstract: Streaming data analytics helps businesses identify opportunities and spot risks in a timely fashion. As large language model (LLM) usage grows, people are exploring incorporating agents or LLMs in streaming data pipelines to help find patterns in datasets without supervision or interpret natural languages for content moderation. However, most streaming systems are currently optimized for data movement and perform poorly on GPU intensive workloads such as performing inference with LLMs. We introduce a system on Google Cloud Dataflow designed to tackle hybrid streaming machine learning workloads with co-designed autoscaling on heterogeneous worker pools and prefix-aware batching. This increases throughput 1.5x to 2x for streaming pipelines using LLMs while maintaining similar latency with up to 75% peak resource savings and 84% lower peak tail latency compared with existing streaming data processing systems.

items.title: Accuracy, Usefulness, and Expert-Perceived Clinical Impact of Response Variability in ChatGPT-4o for Hyperlipidemia-Related Questions
items.abstract: ChatGPT-4o, an advanced Artificial Intelligence based large language model, has demonstrated utility for providing medical information. Data regarding its accuracy and usefulness for hyperlipidemia pharmacotherapy are limited. Additionally, the clinical implications of variability in responses generated from simultaneous identical prompts across multiple sessions remains poorly understood. This research aimed to (1) assess accuracy, (2) evaluate usefulness, and (3) examine perceived impact variability of ChatGPT-4o generated responses to hyperlipidemia-related clinical questions. Five questions addressing hyperlipidemia management and patient counseling were developed. Responses to the questions were collected simultaneously from three independent ChatGPT-4o sessions initiated in separate, newly opened ChatGPT windows. A modified Delphi technique using clinical pharmacy faculty evaluated responses for accuracy, usefulness, and impact variability. Scores were evaluated using a 3-point Likert scale. After initial scoring, responses were collected, collated, and redistributed to faculty for review and optional revision. Final evaluations and consensus were facilitated by a moderator during a virtual panel. Consensus was reached for all responses. Evaluations of response accuracy ranged from poor to good, while usefulness ranged between somewhat useful and very useful. Impact variability ranged from none to high across responses, which faculty concluded could impact patient management. Response variability may have potential clinical implications; however, the present study evaluated expert-perceived potential impact rather than actual patient outcomes. Users should be aware concurrently generated ChatGPT responses can differ in accuracy and usefulness. Clinical judgment and patient-centered multidisciplinary collaboration remain essential. Future directions include using a larger data set to corroborate findings.

items.title: ACTUALIZATION OF THEORETICAL PRINCIPLES AND PRACTICAL TOOLS OF SELF-MANAGEMENT IN MODERN CONDITIONS
items.abstract: The article examines problems in the field of self-management of individual activities and outlines new vectors of research in this field, which are formed under the influence of modern realities. The author summarizes the most common approaches to interpreting the essence and content of self-management, and makes a conditional division of these definitions into two groups: the first involves considering self-management exclusively in the context of the employee's professional development, and the second considers the possibility of using self-management methods and techniques to achieve various goals in different areas of life. The set of factors whose influence on the activities and professional development of a modern person contributes to the actualization of the principles and techniques of self-management is outlined. Attention is paid to the issues of the effectiveness of personal activity planning, the choice of methods for developing one's own work plans, the selection of working tools for optimizing labor efforts and time costs. Also, a set of issues and problems that traditionally belong to the subject of scientific research in the field of self-management is identified, and they are compared with modern issues, which are determined by the new conditions of activity formed by the information society. The existence of a close relationship between the classical and modern issues of the science of self-management is emphasized, which is manifested in changing the aspects of considering traditional issues, and not in the formation of fundamentally new questions for scientific research. It is emphasized that the uncertainty and instability of the external environment puts the development of stress resistance of the employee as a key quality at the forefront among the issues of modern self-management. The author of the article also touches on such an issue as the integration of digital tools and artificial intelligence technologies into the self-management system, characterizes specific practical problems that arise for employees who introduce such technologies to improve the planning and organization of personal activities. The need for further scientific research in the field of self-management and strengthening the applied value of such research to ensure the comprehensive development of each person as an individual is emphasized.
